intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval heart of Prague, wandering through Old Town Square and watching the famous Orloj Astronomical Clock chime on the hour. Discover Gothic churches, Baroque palaces, and hidden cobblestone lanes with a local guide who brings centuries of history to life.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic neo-Baroque Széchenyi thermal baths, one of Europe's largest spa complexes fed by natural geothermal springs. A quintessential Budapest ritual blending relaxation, local culture, and 19th-century grandeur — beloved by locals and travelers alike.

experiences.name: Budapest Great Market Hall Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Hungarian culinary culture at the stunning 1897 Great Market Hall. Sample lángos (deep-fried flatbread), chimney cake, paprika-spiced sausages, and local cheeses while chatting with vendors. A feast for the senses and a true taste of authentic Budapest street food.
experiences.location: Central Market Hall, Fővám tér, Budapest

experiences.name: Prague Czech Cuisine Cooking Class & Beer Pairing
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a traditional Prague kitchen to prepare svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce), trdelník, and other Czech classics. Pair your meal with locally brewed Czech pilsner and learn the cultural stories behind each dish from a passionate local chef.

experiences.name: Danube River Sunset Cruise with Budapest Panorama
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube River at golden hour for breathtaking views of the illuminated Hungarian Parliament, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. This scenic cruise offers a unique waterfront perspective of Budapest's UNESCO-listed riverbank, with optional wine and local snacks on board.
experiences.location: Danube Riverfront, Vigadó tér Pier, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Airport Express Bus (Line 119) to Nádraží Veleslavín metro station, then Metro Line A to Staroměstská station — total cost ~50 CZK (~€2). Check into your boutique stay in Staré Město (Old Town). Once settled, take a leisurely orientation walk through Old Town Square, admire the Gothic Týn Church and the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj). Watch the clock's hourly show if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge at golden hour for stunning views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Explore the atmospheric lanes of Malá Strana just across the bridge. Return to Old Town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and cheap Trdelník (chimney cake) or a fresh sandwich from a local bakery near Old Town Square for ~50–80 CZK (~€2–3).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33, Old Town) — a beloved Czech pub with authentic food. Try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~180–250 CZK (~€7–10). Pair with a cheap Pilsner Urquell draft.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — focus on settling in, getting oriented, and recovering from travel. Buy a 24-hour public transport pass for ~120 CZK (~€5) to use the metro and trams freely.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a hearty Czech breakfast at a local café, then head to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (free to enter the nave), Golden Lane (cobblestone alley with tiny colorful houses), and the Old Royal Palace. Buy a Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK / ~€10) to cover the key highlights. Take Tram 22 from Náměstí Republiky to Pražský hrad stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Visit the Baroque Wallenstein Garden (free entry) and the Church of St. Nicholas. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the Josefov Jewish Quarter from the outside (synagogues visible from the street for free; interior tickets are pricey at ~550 CZK but worth it for history lovers).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for a more local, less touristy evening. Visit a classic Czech hospoda (pub) for beer and conversation with locals.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (Národní 22) or a local pekárna (bakery) — grab a párek v rohlíku (hot dog in a roll) or pastry for ~40–60 CZK (~€1.50–2.50).
meals.lunch: Eat at a local jídelna (canteen-style lunch spot) near Malá Strana — try U Kocoura or a similar spot for a full Czech lunch (soup + main) for ~120–160 CZK (~€5–6).
meals.dinner: Pivovarský klub (Křižíkova 17, Žižkov) — a craft beer pub with solid Czech food. Dinner + beer for ~200–280 CZK (~€8–11).

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid peak crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the castle district involves a lot of uphill walking on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) area — a grand boulevard with historical significance (site of the 1989 Velvet Revolution). Walk to the National Museum at the top of the square (entry ~200 CZK / ~€8). Explore exhibits on Czech natural history and national identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Tram 17 along the Vltava riverbank to the Nusle Bridge area and explore Vyšehrad — a historic fortress and park on a cliff above the river. Visit the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Dvořák and Smetana), the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, and enjoy panoramic city views. Entry to grounds is free; basilica entry ~50 CZK (~€2).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a final Prague evening. Walk the illuminated Old Town Square at night — magical atmosphere. Browse the evening market stalls for affordable snacks.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh rohlik (bread roll) with butter and ham from a supermarket like Albert or Billa near Old Town for ~30–50 CZK (~€1–2).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — a beloved butcher-deli with incredible open-faced sandwiches and Czech meats for ~100–150 CZK (~€4–6). Standing room only — very local.
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Provaznice (Provaznická 3, Old Town) — traditional Czech restaurant with generous portions at fair prices. Main course ~180–230 CZK (~€7–9).

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is far less crowded than Prague Castle and offers equally stunning views — a hidden gem for budget travelers. Pack a light jacket for September evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free for any missed Prague sights or a slow breakfast. Pack your bag and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Train Station) left luggage lockers (~60–100 CZK / ~€2.50–4 for a few hours). Take a final walk through Old Town and the Havelské tržiště (Havel's Market) — a street market selling fruits, vegetables, and Czech souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest. Trains depart from Praha hlavní nádraží and take approximately 6.5–7 hours; buses take ~7–8 hours. RegioJet is highly recommended — comfortable, with free coffee and snacks on some routes. Book in advance for as low as €15–25 one way. Departure ideally around 12:00–14:00, arriving in Budapest by evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Déli railway station). Take the Metro M2 or M4 to your accommodation area. Do a brief walk around your neighborhood to get oriented — grab dinner near the station.

meals.breakfast: Final Czech breakfast — visit a local café for a classic snídaně (breakfast set) with eggs, cheese, and coffee for ~120–160 CZK (~€5–6).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the train: grab a baguette, fruit, and drinks from a supermarket near the train station (~80–120 CZK / ~€3–5). RegioJet also sells affordable snacks onboard.
meals.dinner: Upon arrival in Budapest, head to a nearby étterem (restaurant). Try Borsodi Söröző or a simple Hungarian bistro near Keleti station for gulyásleves (goulash soup) + main for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest train/bus ticket well in advance (at least 2–3 weeks) for the best budget prices. RegioJet is the most budget-friendly and comfortable option. Confirm your Budapest accommodation address before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Begin exploring Budapest with a walk through the historic Belváros (Inner City) district. Visit the stunning St. Stephen's Basilica (free entry to the main nave; panoramic dome climb ~800 HUF / ~€2). Walk to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building along the Danube promenade for exterior photos — one of Europe's most beautiful neo-Gothic buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the famous Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Buda side. Hike up to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) — the Royal Palace complex. Explore the castle grounds, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion (free outer terrace; inner tower ~1,000 HUF / ~€2.50) for breathtaking panoramic views of Pest and the Danube.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Fisherman's Bastion or Castle Hill. Head back to Pest via tram or on foot. Explore the lively Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) area — closes at 18:00 on Saturdays, so time accordingly. Walk through the Jewish Quarter (VII District) and the famous ruin bar district.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local pékség (bakery) for a fresh kifli (crescent roll) and coffee — ~600–900 HUF (~€1.50–2.50).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok, Fővám tér 1–3) — upstairs food stalls serve authentic lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) for ~1,200–1,500 HUF (~€3–4). Incredibly filling and iconic.
meals.dinner: Kádár Étkezde (Klauzál tér 9, Jewish Quarter) — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian lunch spot also open evenings on weekends. Authentic Jewish-Hungarian cuisine for ~2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5–8) per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to visit the Great Market Hall before it closes. The Jewish Quarter comes alive on Friday and Saturday evenings — perfect for exploring the famous ruin bars like Szimpla Kert.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park — one of Budapest's most iconic experiences. Entry for a basic cabin ticket is ~8,000–9,000 HUF (~€20–23). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor thermal pools, a uniquely Hungarian experience. Arrive early (by 9:00) to beat the Sunday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Városliget (City Park) adjacent to the baths — it's free and beautiful in September. Visit Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — both are free and historically significant. Take the historic Millennium Underground (Metro M1, the oldest metro in continental Europe) back toward the center.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side at dusk — the illuminated Buda Castle and Chain Bridge are spectacular. Visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial (free) — a powerful Holocaust memorial made of iron shoes.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast near your accommodation — yogurt, fruit, and coffee from a supermarket (Lidl, Aldi, or Spar) for ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Eat near City Park — Műcsarnok Café or a simple stand in the park for a quick meal. Alternatively, pack sandwiches from a supermarket to eat in the park (~1,000–1,500 HUF / ~€2.50–4).
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király utca 55, VII District) — a beloved, old-school Hungarian kifőzde (home-style canteen). Enormous portions of traditional food at rock-bottom prices. Full dinner ~2,000–2,800 HUF (~€5–7).

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and a towel for the thermal baths (or rent towels on-site for an extra fee). Sunday is a popular day for locals at the baths — arrive early to secure a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) — entry ~2,000 HUF (~€5). Excellent exhibits on Hungarian history from prehistoric times to the 20th century. Afterward, explore the Erzsébetváros (Elizabeth Town / VII District) Jewish Quarter on foot — visit the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue), the largest in Europe. Entry ~5,000 HUF (~€13) but deeply moving and historically significant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the hip Kazinczy Street area and surrounding ruin bar neighborhood in daylight — great for photography and café culture. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for an exterior look (interior tours available ~3,500 HUF / ~€9 if interested). Walk Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene. Start at Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy utca 14) — the original ruin bar, open every night. Have a few local Dreher or Borsodi beers (~600–900 HUF / ~€1.50–2.50 each). Free to enter most nights.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at a local kávéház (coffeehouse) — try Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square for the atmosphere (splurge ~2,000–2,500 HUF / ~€5–6) or a simpler café nearby for ~1,000–1,500 HUF (~€2.50–4).
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (multiple locations in VII District) — a Budapest institution offering generous, affordable Middle Eastern food beloved by locals and students. Full meal ~1,800–2,500 HUF (~€4.50–6.50).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner before the ruin bars — grab a lángos or kürtőskalács from a street vendor (~800–1,200 HUF / ~€2–3), or eat at a simple pizza/kebab spot in the Jewish Quarter.

day_by_day.notes: If you're a fan of opera or classical music, check the Hungarian State Opera House website for last-minute standing room tickets — sometimes available for as little as €5. Monday evenings are less crowded at ruin bars than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — take a leisurely walk along the Danube on the Buda side. Visit the Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic view of the entire city. Hike up (free) or take a tram partway. Visit the Citadella fortress at the top and the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) — both free and iconic. Descend via the Gellért Baths side if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your accommodation, check out, and store luggage. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Hold Street Market (Hold utcai Vásárcsarnok) — more local and less touristy than the Great Market Hall. Pick up Hungarian paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), and Tokaji wine as affordable gifts. Head to the airport or train station for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most historic and beautiful cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — visit a local eszpresszó (espresso bar) for coffee and a pogácsa (savory scone) or rétes (strudel) for ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Grab a final hearty Hungarian meal before departure. Étterem Klassz (Andrássy út 41) offers a great value lunch menu, or try a simple soup and main at any neighborhood étterem for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — pack snacks from a local supermarket to save money (~1,000–1,500 HUF / ~€2.50–4).

day_by_day.notes: Budapest Airport (BUD) is connected by the 100E express bus from Deák Ferenc tér — costs ~1,100 HUF (~€3) and takes ~30–35 minutes. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for travel and check-in. September is a beautiful month in both cities — mild temperatures (15–22°C) and fewer crowds than summer.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or Uber to your boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí). Watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour, admire the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn, and soak in the medieval atmosphere. Walk across the iconic Charles Bridge for your first views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the charming lanes of Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) at dusk, then settle into a cozy Czech restaurant for your first local dinner. Enjoy a relaxed evening getting acquainted with the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — nothing formal scheduled.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre-style bistro near Old Town or a quick stop at a local bakery (pekárna) for an open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) — budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Prague gastropub in Old Town serving traditional Czech cuisine: svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce), roast pork knee, and perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell. Budget ~€15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a transit card (Lítačka) at the airport or a metro station for easy movement around the city. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so pack a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), and enjoy panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops. Arrive early (9:00) to beat the crowds. Budget ~2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — Prague's baroque neighborhood. Visit the stunning St. Nicholas Church, wander the quiet cobblestone streets, and stop at Kampa Island for a peaceful riverside walk. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the bridge towers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for a more local, less touristy evening. Browse the lively bar scene or attend a classical music concert — Prague is renowned for affordable evening concerts in historic churches and halls.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or grab coffee and a fresh croissant at Café Savoy near Malá Strana — one of Prague's most beautiful historic cafés. Budget ~€6–10.
meals.lunch: Malostranská Beseda restaurant in Malá Strana — hearty Czech lunch specials (polední menu) including soup + main for ~€8–12. Excellent value.
meals.dinner: Kantýna in Vinohrady — a beloved modern Czech butcher-restaurant known for quality meats, house-made sausages, and natural wines. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle requires a combined ticket (~€14–18 for the full circuit). Book online in advance to skip queues. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the castle district involves significant uphill walking on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) in depth — visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial. This is one of the most historically significant Jewish heritage sites in Europe. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river to the Letná district. Visit the National Technical Museum or simply walk through Letná Park for sweeping panoramic views of the city and the Vltava River. Rent a bike or relax at the famous Letná Beer Garden (Letenský zámeček) — a local favorite with stunning views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a final Prague evening. Explore the Náplavka riverbank area if time permits, then enjoy dinner in the Nové Město (New Town) area for a slightly more local vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery in Karlín (short tram ride) — one of Prague's most celebrated modern bakeries with exceptional sourdough, pastries, and specialty coffee. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Letná Beer Garden — classic Czech beer (Kozel or Staropramen on tap) with goulash or grilled sausage. Casual, affordable, and scenic. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Maso a Kobliha (Meat & Doughnut) — a quirky, beloved Prague spot known for creative Czech-inspired dishes and craft beer. Lively atmosphere, great for solo travelers or couples. Budget ~€15–20.

day_by_day.notes: Josefov combined ticket covers 6 synagogues + the cemetery (~€20–25). The cemetery is especially moving — approach it with respect. This is your last full day in Prague; consider picking up any souvenirs (avoid Old Town Square tourist traps — try Manufaktura for quality Czech crafts).

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Prague hotel and take the morning train from Praha Hlavní Nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti Station. The RegioJet or CD/MÁV direct train takes approximately 6.5–7 hours — a scenic journey through Czech and Slovak countryside. Book seats in advance for comfort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the late afternoon (~19:00–20:00 depending on train). Transfer to your Budapest accommodation. Freshen up and take a short orientation walk through your neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — take a gentle walk along the Danube embankment (the Pest side) to see the illuminated Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle lit up at night. One of the most spectacular urban nightscapes in Europe.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Prague hotel or grab pastries and coffee to go before heading to the train station.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or purchase food at the train station — RegioJet trains have a bistro car with sandwiches, snacks, and drinks. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Arrive hungry in Budapest — head to Belvárosi Disznótoros or a nearby Hungarian tavern for your first taste of Budapest: goulash soup, lángos (fried dough), and Hungarian craft beer. Budget ~€14–20.

day_by_day.notes: The Prague–Budapest train is a highlight of the trip — book 1st class for ~€40–60 for a comfortable, scenic ride. Alternatively, a FlixBus is cheaper (~€15–25) but takes longer. Keep your passport handy as the train passes through Slovakia. September is peak travel season — book train tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from the Chain Bridge. Visit Buda Castle (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion with its fairy-tale turrets and extraordinary panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Allow 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge on foot back to Pest. Walk along Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard) toward Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument. Explore City Park (Városliget) and the exterior of Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar scene — Szimpla Kert in the Jewish Quarter is the original and most iconic. A labyrinthine, eclectic bar built inside a crumbling building, filled with local art, live music, and an electric atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — Budapest's most ornate and legendary café, often called 'the most beautiful café in the world.' Splurge slightly on coffee and pastries here for the experience. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen near the Chain Bridge — Michelin Bib Gourmand Hungarian cuisine with excellent local wines. Budget ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Street food at Szimpla Kert or nearby Jewish Quarter eateries — falafel, lángos, chimney cake (kürtőskalács). Budget ~€8–12.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Budapest is lively — Szimpla Kert hosts a popular farmers' market on Saturday mornings if you're up early. The Jewish Quarter (District VII) is the heart of Budapest's cultural and nightlife scene — explore it thoroughly today and tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most atmospheric indoor market. Three floors of fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, sausages, embroidery, and folk crafts. A feast for the senses. Then walk to the stunning Hungarian Parliament Building for an interior tour (book in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and rejuvenate at the Széchenyi Thermal Baths — Budapest's most famous outdoor thermal bath complex in City Park. Soak in the iconic yellow neo-baroque pools, try the steam rooms and saunas. A quintessential Budapest experience. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — a 1-hour boat tour gives you unparalleled views of both riverbanks, the Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle illuminated at dusk. Then dinner in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh langos or a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) from the Great Market Hall vendors — the most authentic Budapest breakfast experience. Budget ~€3–6.
meals.lunch: Karavan Street Food Court near Szimpla Kert — an outdoor food truck park with Hungarian and international street food options. Try the chimney cake ice cream. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Macesz Huszár — a celebrated Hungarian-Jewish restaurant in the Jewish Quarter serving traditional recipes like cholent, stuffed cabbage, and matzo-based dishes. Budget ~€18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online well in advance — especially on weekends. Széchenyi Baths entry is ~€25–30; bring a towel or rent one on-site. The Danube sunset cruise costs ~€15–25 depending on the operator — look for operators on Vigadó tér pier.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving Holocaust memorial site. The adjacent Jewish Museum and the Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Garden are equally powerful. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Then walk through the charming Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Courtyard) — a series of connected courtyards filled with cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hungarian National Museum for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Hungarian history, culture, and art. Then head to Váci Street and the Inner City for some window shopping and exploration. Walk along the Danube promenade (Duna-korzó) for beautiful river views.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music or opera performance — the Hungarian State Opera House is one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe and tickets are surprisingly affordable. Alternatively, enjoy a wine-tasting evening at a local wine bar specializing in Tokaj and Eger wines.

meals.breakfast: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — a Budapest institution since 1858. Try the iconic Gerbeaud cake (layered walnut and apricot jam sponge). Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Első Pesti Rétesház — the 'First Strudel House of Pest,' serving sweet and savory Hungarian strudels (rétes). Excellent value and authentically local. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Stand25 Bisztró — a modern Hungarian bistro run by a Michelin-starred chef offering elevated Hungarian cuisine at mid-range prices. Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hungarian State Opera House tickets range from ~€5 (standing) to ~€50 (premium seats) — book at the box office or online. Even if opera isn't your thing, the building's interior is worth a guided tour (~€10). This is your last full day in Budapest — make the most of it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — take a peaceful walk through Margaret Island (Margitsziget) in the middle of the Danube. A car-free green oasis with rose gardens, medieval ruins, a musical fountain, and joggers. Perfect for a relaxed farewell morning. Alternatively, revisit a favorite spot or explore any missed neighborhoods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time — check out of your hotel and make your way to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) or the train/bus station. Allow at least 2 hours before a flight departure. Pick up last-minute Hungarian souvenirs: Tokaj wine, Pick salami, Unicum liqueur, or Herend porcelain.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a local café near your hotel — try Espresso Embassy or Brew Your Mind for world-class specialty coffee and pastries. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Quick but quality farewell meal — Buja Disznó or a nearby Hungarian lunchroom (étkezde) for a hearty final bowl of gulyás (goulash) soup and fresh bread. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Margaret Island is free to enter and reachable by bus (26) or on foot across Margaret Bridge. Budapest Airport is ~30 minutes from the city center by the 100E airport bus (direct, ~€3) or taxi (~€25–30). Allow extra time on Tuesday mornings due to potential business travel congestion at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury chauffeur service to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most), admire the 30 Baroque statues, and take in sweeping views of the Vltava River. Continue into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana) for a leisurely exploration of cobblestone lanes and Baroque architecture. Visit the Church of St. Nicholas for a quick cultural stop.
day_by_day.evening: Evening walk through the Old Town Square to witness the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and soak in the golden-hour atmosphere of the medieval square. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif at a rooftop bar overlooking the Old Town rooftops.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Late lunch at Café Savoy — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café serving refined Czech cuisine; try the svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and house-baked pastries.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Field Restaurant (1 Michelin Star) — innovative Czech tasting menu using seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for a world-class introduction to modern Bohemian cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for jet lag recovery and acclimatization. Confirm Field Restaurant reservation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) visit — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral with its stunning Gothic stained glass, the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the charming Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Hire a private licensed guide for an in-depth 3-hour experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the picturesque Nerudova Street into Malá Strana. Visit the Wallenstein Palace and its baroque garden — a hidden gem of Prague. Continue to the Kampa Island area and explore the open-air Kampa Museum of modern Central European art.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert at the Lobkowicz Palace or the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — both offer world-class chamber music performances in breathtaking historical settings. Pre-concert drinks in the ornate café of the Municipal House.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or at Café Louvre — a historic literary café serving Viennese-style breakfast with freshly baked bread, cold cuts, eggs, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Coda Restaurant (inside the Aria Hotel, Malá Strana) — rooftop terrace with panoramic castle views; contemporary European cuisine with a refined Czech touch.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Dégustation Bohême Bourgeoise (1 Michelin Star) — an extraordinary 6 or 11-course tasting menu celebrating the forgotten flavors of historical Bohemian cuisine. One of Prague's most prestigious dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private castle guide at least 2 weeks in advance. Concert tickets at Municipal House should be reserved ahead of time — September is peak cultural season in Prague.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Old-New Synagogue (the oldest active synagogue in Europe), the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial, and the Maisel Synagogue. A private guided tour is highly recommended for historical depth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, then explore the National Museum on Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí). Browse the luxury boutiques and galleries along Pařížská Street — Prague's most prestigious shopping boulevard — for Czech crystal, Bohemian garnets, and designer fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise on the Vltava aboard a private luxury boat. Enjoy champagne and canapés as you glide past illuminated landmarks including Charles Bridge, Prague Castle, and the National Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Eska — a celebrated bakery-restaurant in Holešovice district (short taxi ride) known for sourdough breads, seasonal preserves, and specialty filter coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved authentic Czech gastropub serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell tank beer and traditional Czech dishes like fried cheese (smažený sýr) and roast pork knee (vepřové koleno).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Collection Alcron Hotel) — Art Deco elegance meets modern European fine dining. Exceptional seafood and Czech-inspired tasting menus in a glamorous 1930s setting.

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter tickets should be purchased in advance online — combination tickets cover all six synagogues and the cemetery. Private Vltava boat cruises can be arranged through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage town approximately 1 hour from Prague by private car. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of up to 70,000 people, and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara (Chrám svaté Barbory), a masterpiece of Bohemian Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague. Check out of Prague hotel and prepare for the journey to Budapest. Board a premium Regiojet or Railjet train from Prague Main Station (Praha hlavní nádraží) to Budapest Keleti — a scenic 6.5 to 7-hour journey through the Bohemian and Slovak countryside. Alternatively, arrange a private luxury car transfer for the full route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest in the early evening. Private transfer to your luxury accommodation in the heart of Budapest (recommended: Párisi Udvar Hotel, Four Seasons Gresham Palace, or Boscolo Budapest). Brief evening stroll along the Danube Promenade to see the illuminated Parliament Building.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab pastries and coffee from a local Prague bakery for an early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Restaurace V Ruthardce — a charming restaurant in the historic center serving traditional Bohemian cuisine in a medieval setting.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Restaurant (1 Michelin Star) — Hungary's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a sophisticated tasting menu blending Hungarian flavors with modern European techniques. A perfect introduction to Budapest's culinary scene.

day_by_day.notes: Kutná Hora requires an early start (depart Prague by 8:30 AM). Book private car transfer for Kutná Hora and for Prague–Budapest leg well in advance. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time given late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda Castle District — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its stunning diamond-patterned roof tiles and ornate interior. Walk to the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most iconic panoramic views over the Danube, the Parliament, and Pest. Hire a private guide for historical context on Hungary's royal and Ottoman history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot into Pest. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the most beautiful parliament buildings in the world — on a guided interior tour. Stroll along Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's grand boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces, luxury boutiques, and embassies.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) — one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe. September marks the opening of the opera season, making this a truly special cultural experience. Enjoy a pre-show glass of Hungarian Tokaji wine in the ornate foyer.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most legendary café and confectionery, serving since 1858. Try the Gerbeaud cake and Hungarian-style pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Halászbástya Restaurant — panoramic terrace dining at the Fisherman's Bastion with refined Hungarian cuisine and extraordinary Danube views.
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Onyx Restaurant (2 Michelin Stars) on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most celebrated fine dining destination, offering a refined Hungarian tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings from the Tokaj and Eger regions.

day_by_day.notes: Opera tickets must be booked well in advance — September opening season performances sell out quickly. Smart formal attire required for the opera. Fisherman's Bastion is best visited early morning to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Thermal spa experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) — Budapest's grandest and most famous thermal spa, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park. Enjoy the outdoor and indoor thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional private massage treatments. A quintessential Budapest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most beautiful indoor market, a stunning iron-and-glass 19th-century structure. Browse stalls selling Hungarian paprika, sausages, Tokaji wine, embroidered textiles, and artisan goods. Continue to the Jewish Quarter (VII District) — explore the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue), the largest in Europe, and the moving Holocaust Memorial Tree of Life.
day_by_day.evening: Ruin bar experience in the Jewish Quarter — visit Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar, for a uniquely Budapest evening atmosphere. Then move to a sophisticated cocktail bar such as Doblo Wine Bar or High Note SkyBar for panoramic night views over the illuminated city.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast to prepare for the spa morning.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen (1 Michelin Star) — exceptional Hungarian wine-focused restaurant with a seasonally changing menu. Perfect pairing of modern Hungarian cuisine with outstanding local wines.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stand Restaurant (2 Michelin Stars) — helmed by celebrated Hungarian chef Szabina Szulló and Tamás Széll, offering a deeply personal and innovative Hungarian tasting menu. One of the most exciting dining experiences in Central Europe.

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Spa private cabin or VIP lounge in advance for a more exclusive experience. Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays — Sunday is ideal. Ruin bars get lively after 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) — one of the largest collections of European art outside of Paris and Vienna, with masterpieces by El Greco, Raphael, Goya, and Rembrandt. Explore the adjacent City Park (Városliget) and the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Danube river cruise on a private luxury boat — cruise past all of Budapest's iconic landmarks including the Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, Matthias Church, and the Citadella. Enjoy afternoon tea and Hungarian wine on board. Alternatively, visit the Hungarian National Museum for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Hungarian history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk across the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) to Gellért Hill — climb to the Citadella fortress for the most spectacular panoramic views of Budapest at dusk, with the entire city and Danube laid out below. Descend for a final elegant evening in the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café — arguably the world's most beautiful café, a gilded Neo-Baroque masterpiece serving lavish Hungarian breakfasts and pastries. An unmissable Budapest landmark.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Babel Budapest Restaurant (1 Michelin Star) — creative Hungarian cuisine in an intimate setting, with a strong focus on seasonal local ingredients and Hungarian wine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Kollázs Brasserie & Bar (inside the Four Seasons Gresham Palace) — stunning Art Nouveau surroundings with sophisticated European brasserie cuisine and an extensive Hungarian wine list. A glamorous final evening in Budapest.

day_by_day.notes: Gellért Hill sunset walk is best done around 6:30–7:00 PM in mid-September. New York Café is popular — book a breakfast reservation in advance. Private Danube cruises can be arranged through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest. Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute exploration of the elegant Váci Street for luxury shopping — Hungarian Tokaji wine, handcrafted leather goods, Herend porcelain, and Zsolnay ceramics make exceptional gifts and souvenirs. Visit the Central Market Hall one last time for any final food purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) for departure. Allow ample time for premium check-in and lounge access.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through the cultural, culinary, and architectural heart of Central Europe.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at your hotel — enjoy a full Hungarian breakfast spread with cold cuts, cheeses, fresh bread, eggs, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Café Gerbeaud or a café near Váci Street — Hungarian lángos (fried dough), chimney cake (kürtőskalács), or a refined soup and sandwich before departure.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining at the Budapest Airport premium lounge.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Consider purchasing Tokaji Aszú wine and Herend porcelain as premium souvenirs — both are uniquely Hungarian luxury items. Keep receipts for potential VAT refund on luxury purchases.
